# A local build guard run through a symlinked path exits 0 without checking anything

## Context

@neo-opus-grace found this in her review of PR #18906 (2026-09-18). I measured it the same day and sent a defect-note. The engine's `buildScripts` guards run their CLI block only when `process.argv[1]` names the module itself. Node resolves symlinks in the entry module's `import.meta.url`, but not in `process.argv[1]`. So a guard run through a symlinked path skips its CLI block and exits 0: a checkout under macOS `/tmp` or `/var`, or any absolute path through a link.

## The Problem

Measured at `dev@02e48cf441`, running each guard once through its real path and once through a symlink to the same checkout. A guard whose CLI block ran prints a report; one whose block never ran prints nothing and exits 0.

| guard | entry check | output, real path | output, symlinked path |
|---|---|---|---|
| `check-fixed-sleeps` | `path.resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` | 306 bytes | **0** |
| `check-file-sizes` | `path.resolve(process.argv[1]) === __filename` | 423 bytes | **0** |
| `check-guard-ci-parity` | `path.resolve(process.argv[1]) === __filename` | 74 bytes | **0** |
| `check-jsdoc-types` | `path.resolve(process.argv[1]) === __filename` | 126 bytes | **0** |
| `check-engine-brain-boundary` | ``import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}` `` | 183 bytes | **0** |

That is a false green from the very command a person or agent runs to check their own change. `lint-staged` and CI invoke the guards by relative path, so the hook and CI are not affected.

`check-class-module-scope.mjs:248-253` tells readers the `path.resolve` form is the fix for symlinks. It is not. Its own spec, `the CLI entry predicate survives a checkout path containing a space`, realpaths the tmpdir precisely because "BOTH predicates" fail through `/tmp`.

## The Architectural Reality

- Every entry check lives in its guard, in about ten spellings. 32 files outside specs in `buildScripts/` and `test/playwright/` gate a CLI block on `process.argv[1]`.
- The `endsWith('<name>.mjs')` spelling (`check-spec-retirement`, `e2eCiSelection`, `flickerCensus`) survives a symlink, but it matches any file of that name.
- **The fix is already written elsewhere.** The published guards in neo-agent-skills (`check-npm-overrides`, `check-substrate-size`, `check-ticket-archaeology`, `check-secrets`) compare `realpathSync()` on both sides. They are tested through the installed `bin` symlink and under `--preserve-symlinks-main`.

## The Fix

- `buildScripts/util/isEntryModule.mjs`: `isEntryModule(import.meta.url)`. It realpaths both sides, and returns false when `process.argv[1]` is missing or unreadable.
- Every entry check in `buildScripts/` and `test/playwright/` calls it, so `git grep 'process.argv\[1\]'` finds only the helper and the specs that probe it.
- `check-class-module-scope`'s comment and its entry-predicate arms follow.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: a unit spec for the helper. Run through the real path, a symlinked path and `--preserve-symlinks-main`, a probe's block runs. Imported by another module, and with no `process.argv[1]`, it does not.
- [ ] AC-2: through a symlinked checkout path, a guard reports again: red on `dev`, where it prints nothing.
- [ ] AC-3: `git grep -n 'process.argv\[1\]' -- buildScripts test/playwright` finds only the helper and specs.

## Out of Scope

- `buildScripts/util/check-secrets.mjs`, which retires in #18929.
- `.claude/hooks/rgReplaceGuardHook.mjs`: harness substrate that the harness invokes by its real path.
